summary: Intermittent dedicated pool throughput collapse during short-lived tenant I/O spikes causing autoscaler starvation
description: Issue summary: Between 2026-03-12 10:40 and 2026-03-12 11:05 UTC the customer's dedicated GPU pool experienced repeated p99/p50 throughput regressions (~40-60% drop) and elevated queue lengths. Impact: NovaMaps reported degraded inference latency for user-facing routing features and elevated error retries. Environment: Dedicated pool backed by rtx-a6000 instances in us-east-1, autoscaler configured with predictive_window=60s, scale_up_cooldown=90s, max_nodes=12. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send sustained short streams (50-200 requests/sec) from a synthetic tenant that creates many small streams with heavy KV-cache churn; 2) Observe autoscaler behavior and GPU attach/detach events. Observed behavior: sudden IO bursts from an ephemeral tenant caused host-level NVMe I/O saturation and delayed GPU attach operations; autoscaler observed perceived capacity shortage and began aggressive scale-up attempts which repeatedly failed due to transient node provisioning delays; meanwhile higher-priority tenant requests were queued which led to throughput collapse. Logs/metrics: - Serving runtime p99 latency spike 10:41 -> 10:47 UTC (from 180ms -> 720ms) - Autoscaler scale_up_attempts: 7 in 6 minutes, 5 timeouts - Node attach error: "attach_timeout: nvme_wait_io_blocked" - NVMe utilization on affected hosts reported at 95% for ~90s - Per-tenant slot occupancy showed one tenant (tenant-id: t-nm-119) occupying many short-lived streams. Impacted customers: NovaMaps (reported), adjacent tenants on same pool experienced reduced throughput but no 5xxs. Temporary workaround: We moved NovaMaps traffic to fallback pool (dedicated-fallback-3) at 11:10 UTC which restored throughput to expected levels.
steps_to_reproduce: Run synthetic client that opens 60-120 short streaming sessions/second with frequent small token outputs (1-8 tokens)
Observe autoscaler logs and pool attach events under same load pattern
Monitor host NVMe and PCIe latency metrics while load is running
investigation_notes: 10:50 UTC - Support (Maya) collected pprof traces and streaming session histograms and escalated to SRE (#support -> #incidents)
11:00 UTC - SRE (Arjun) observed pattern: IO-heavy prefetch + frequent short sessions correlated with NVMe queues spiking on a subset of hosts leading to attach timeouts

11:05 UTC - Hypothesis A: short-lived streams with aggressive prefetch are causing host IO saturation and blocking the attach path for new GPU containers. Hypothesis B: autoscaler predictive window too short causing over-aggressive scale attempts that collide with provisioning limits.
11:20 UTC - Corroboration: kernel logs show repeated blk-mq timeouts and dmesg entries 'nvme_io_timeout' on hosts h-us-e-042..047; correlated to tenants with >200 small streams/minute.

11:35 UTC - Investigated scheduler allocation: packing policy allowed many short streams to multiplex into same GPU slot which increased IO fanout; eviction metrics show frequent micro-evictions for background checkpoint writer on same hosts.
12:10 UTC - Reproduced in staging by replaying customer's traffic pattern; reproduced NVMe saturation and attach_timeout within 30s of traffic starting.

12:30 UTC - Temporary mitigation: increased autoscaler scale_up_cooldown to 180s and throttled prefetch_count for suspected tenant via per-tenant config. Observed immediate reduction in attach failures but throughput still suboptimal until traffic migrated.
13:00 UTC - Follow-up action items documented and handed to infra team for longer-term fixes (see related PRs and runbook updates).

resolution_notes: Workaround: We migrated NovaMaps off the contaminated host set to dedicated-fallback-3 which restored throughput. Short-term mitigations applied: throttle prefetch_count for tenant t-nm-119, increased autoscaler scale_up_cooldown to 180s to reduce thrash, and temporarily disabled background checkpoint writer scheduling on serving hosts. Long-term actions: (1) infra PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1428 to add NVMe-aware placement constraints and avoid scheduling heavy IO background jobs on serving nodes, (2) autoscaler change: add request-rate aware predictive windowing and backoff on repeated attach failures, (3) per-tenant prefetch/IO quota enforcement and telemetry to detect noisy-tenant patterns early, (4) update runbook at https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Dedicated+Pool+Noisy+Tenant+Runbook. Owner for infra fixes: Sophie Nguyen. Owner for autoscaler tuning: Arjun Patel. Expected follow-up timeline: infra PR to land by 2026-03-20, autoscaler tuning staged in canary by 2026-03-18.

Autoscaler: implement attach-failure backoff and request-rate predictive window changes in beta

Customer follow-up: inform NovaMaps of planned infra/autoscaler changes and coordinate maintenance windows if needed
final_status_notes: Ticket remains In Progress while infra and autoscaler changes are tracked. Customer traffic is currently on fallback pool with no further impact reported as of 2026-03-14. Will move to Resolved after PRs merged and canary verification completes.
